subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: For LiteLLM/Vertex beta 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` without token-limit wording, should OpenClaw treat the error as provider-owned conversation-state recovery, context compaction/fallback, or only improved diagnostics until a live repro proves the wedge?
rationale: Current source shows the classification gap, but the correct behavior changes provider failover and session-recovery semantics and needs maintainer intent plus live provider evidence.

options.title: Require live repro before coding
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a live LiteLLM Vertex beta reproduction that captures the redacted error object and session lane state before choosing the recovery path.

options.title: Provider-owned classifier
options.body: Add a narrow LiteLLM or Google Vertex plugin hook for this exact error shape and map it to an actionable conversation-state or format failure without broad core matching.

options.title: Broader session recovery
options.body: Treat generic provider `INVALID_ARGUMENT` as a session recovery trigger, accepting a higher risk of misclassifying unrelated provider validation errors.

recommendation.title: Require live repro before coding
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a live LiteLLM Vertex beta reproduction that captures the redacted error object and session lane state before choosing the recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged and recently carried the adjacent provider-error classification and auto-reply recovery surfaces that need the product-direction decision.
